chunks: From him, from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Yahya ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Ali (peace be upon him) would not fight until the sun set, and he would say, 'The gates of heaven are opened, mercy descends, and victory comes down.' And he would say, 'It is closer to night and more likely that killing will decrease, the pursuer will return, and the defeated will escape.'
ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali delay fighting until sunset according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith highlights Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) strategic patience, balancing spiritual optimism with military pragmatism. By delaying battle until sunset, he not only invoked divine favor but also minimized bloodshed, allowing the defeated to retreat rather than face annihilation, a practice reflecting the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) in warfare.
